questions: When the board is fully in view, are there exactly three pens on it (no missing pen and no empty gap)?
Do all three pens point the same direction, with none flipped or reversed relative to the other two?
Are all three pens the same color as each other, with none differing in color?
Is every pen complete and capped, with none showing a bare/exposed writing tip or looking clearly shorter than the others?
Does the board move smoothly and continuously from left to right, without stopping, freezing, pausing, reversing, or jamming at any point?

question_answers.evidence: When the board is fully in the frame (around 00:07-00:10), there are clearly three pens visible on the white board.
The two leftmost pens are vertical and parallel, but the rightmost pen is tilted diagonally. They are not all aligned in the same direction.
All three pens appear to have the same translucent barrel and black cap/end, indicating they are the same color.
All three pens appear to have the black cap at one end and look to be of similar length; none clearly shows a bare tip or looks significantly shorter.
The board moves continuously from left to right across the frame without stopping or reversing.

parsed.reason: The rightmost pen is tilted diagonally relative to the other two vertical pens, meaning the pens are not all aligned in the same direction as required for the NORMAL condition.

description: One pen is flipped relative to the others (variant).
